claims.text: Ultra-high-vacuum, low-strain-rate decomposition will keep oxygen below the critical solubility limit.
Keeping oxygen below the critical solubility limit will suppress brittle alpha-HCP and TiO precipitates.
Thermomechanical extrusion will refine the grain structure and thereby improve high-temperature yield strength without catastrophic cracking.
Hydride-derived Group-IV-containing RHEA powders may initially contain approximately 1.0 wt% oxygen because of mechanical alloying or hydride handling.
The precursor powder has a nanocrystalline or fine-grained microstructure.
A low-temperature decomposition stage followed by high-temperature, high-pressure extrusion can remove hydrogen, manage oxygen diffusion, and densify the alloy without brittle fracture.
An atmosphere below 10^-6 Pa is required to prevent further oxygen uptake.
Extrusion must occur above the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature but below the onset of rapid Laves-phase precipitation.
A low strain rate during the decomposition-to-densification transition permits stress relaxation and avoids brittle failure.
Grain-boundary oxygen segregation is a structural mediator of the proposed response.
Kinetic control of diffusion and strain-induced grain refinement suppresses coherent alpha-HCP and TiO nucleation.
Low-strain-rate decomposition releases hydrogen without producing local stresses that drive oxygen uptake and brittle-phase precipitation.
Stepwise thermomechanical processing can produce a single-phase BCC structure or controlled coherent precipitation through high-configurational-entropy stabilization.
The adapted process will produce a dense, crack-free bulk material with a significantly reduced transition temperature.
The processed material will retain high yield strength up to 700°C because of grain refinement and the absence of brittle grain-boundary precipitates.
The processed material will have greater ductility than as-cast counterparts.
Preparation of NbMoTaWVTi introduces interstitial oxygen and can form an unintended TiO precipitate.
Brittle Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries can reduce plasticity and promote cracking.
High Cr or Si content can inherently favor Laves-phase formation regardless of oxygen control.
Low strain rate or higher processing temperature may permit hot deformation of oxygen-rich HfNbTaTiZr.
